mainTopic: Does רב hold like רבי שמעון that a דבר שאין מתכוין (an unintended result) is permitted on יום טוב? This comes up in the case of clearing hair from the slaughter spot with a cleaver.
overview: The amud opens with the last word of רב's ruling: on יום טוב one may clear hair from the slaughter spot with a cleaver, even though some hair may be pulled out. The גמרא first challenges this from רב's strict ruling on a barrel stopper. It answers that the stopper is a פסיק רישיה, which even רבי שמעון forbids. Next comes a stronger challenge: רב is reported to rule like רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין. So the גמרא explains רב differently. Plucking is not shearing, and on יום טוב the plucking is done כלאחר יד. This leads to a long back-and-forth about רבי יוסי בן המשולם and the פרה אדומה, ending with two answers. Either a פרה אדומה is rare, or רבי יוסי בן המשולם does not share רב's view. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rules: hair may be plucked only by hand, not with a tool, and plucking hair to show a מום is allowed לכתחילה. Finally a new משנה begins about hair that fell off a בכור בעל מום before slaughter. עקביא בן מהללאל permits it, and the opposing view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of רב's ruling: it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: This word finishes רב's ruling from the previous section. Clearing hair from the slaughter spot with a cleaver on יום טוב is permitted, even though some hair may get plucked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This single word finishes רב's ruling on the previous amud. He says it is allowed to clear hair from the slaughter spot on יום טוב, even if some hair gets pulled out by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling out hair would normally be a forbidden מלאכה. רב permits it here because the person does not intend to pluck; he only wants to clear the spot for a proper שחיטה. That follows the view of רבי שמעון that a דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted
An action whose forbidden result the person does not intend
A Festival day

phrases.english: It is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the last word of רב's ruling, which began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of רב that was cited at the end of the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clearing hair at the slaughter spot on יום טוב is permitted, even though some hair may be plucked unintentionally.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's ruling on the barrel stopper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב could permit this. Elsewhere רב forbids pushing a cloth stopper tightly into a barrel on יום טוב, which shows he forbids unintended results.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say this? But רב חייא בר אשי said in רב's name: it is forbidden to push in a barrel's cloth stopper tightly on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's lenient ruling by quoting a strict ruling of his in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing a cloth stopper in tightly squeezes liquid out of the cloth. Squeezing is forbidden on יום טוב, even though the person did not intend it. If רב forbids that unintended squeezing, it seems he should also forbid the unintended plucking of hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רב really say this? (a formula introducing a contradiction)
A cloth stopper or plug
A barrel
To push it in tightly

phrases.english: And did Rav really say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi say in the name of Rav:
the cloth stopper of a barrel
it is forbidden to push it in tightly on a Festival!
phrases.notes: The reason is that liquid gets squeezed out of the cloth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 1 using a contradictory ruling of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the unintended plucking of hair is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids the unintended squeezing from a stopper, so he should also forbid the unintended plucking of hair.

steps.title: The stopper is a case of inevitable result
steps.stepSummary: The stopper case is different because the squeezing will definitely happen. That makes it a פסיק רישיה, which even רבי שמעון forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case, even רבי שמעון agrees it is forbidden. As אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and won't it die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the stopper case is in a different category from the hair case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits an unintended result only when it might not happen. With a tight cloth stopper, liquid will certainly be squeezed out. That is a פסיק רישיה, so it is forbidden even according to רבי שמעון. The hair might not get plucked at all, so רב can still permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: In that case
Agrees or concedes
Both of them
'Cut off its head and won't it die?', meaning an unintended result that is certain to happen

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון permits every unintended act. He forbids it whenever the forbidden result is certain, which is called פסיק רישיה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that even רבי שמעון forbids a פסיק רישיה is a basic principle in הלכות שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: In that case, even Rabbi Shimon agrees,
as Abaye and Rava both say:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head and won't it die?'
phrases.notes: This means a case where the forbidden result is inevitable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by distinguishing the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (inevitable result versus possible result)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's strict ruling on the stopper seemed to show that he forbids every unintended act.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stopper is a פסיק רישיה, which is forbidden even according to רבי שמעון. רב can therefore still hold like רבי שמעון when the result is not certain.

steps.title: Challenge: רב explicitly rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a stronger challenge. Two separate reports say רב ruled הלכה like רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין, while שמואל ruled like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חייא בר אשי said in רב's name: the הלכה is like רבי יהודה. And רב חנן בר אמי said in שמואל's name: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון. And רב חייא בר אבין taught it without naming the transmitters: רב said the הלכה is like רבי יהודה, and שמואל said the הלכה is like רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. רב is on record ruling like רבי יהודה, the strict view, so how could he permit the unintended plucking of hair? The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge is not about one case. It quotes רב's general ruling on the whole מחלוקת. Two independent chains of transmission confirm that רב follows רבי יהודה, who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין. That directly contradicts the lenient ruling in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows (someone's view)
Teaches or transmits
Without naming the people who passed on the ruling
The תנא who forbids a דבר שאין מתכוין

steps.whatToRemember: רב permitted clearing the hair, and the stopper case was answered by the rule of פסיק רישיה. But now רב's own general ruling like רבי יהודה stands against him. Step 5 answers this with a new explanation of רב.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi say that Rav said:
the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥanan bar Ami said that Shmuel said:
the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מַתְנֵי בְּלָא גַּבְרֵי:
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin teaches it without naming the transmitters:
Rav said the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and Shmuel said the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 defended רב as following רבי שמעון, this step challenges that assumption directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רב follows רבי שמעון on a דבר שאין מתכוין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two independent reports say רב ruled like רבי יהודה, who forbids unintended acts. So רב should not permit the unintended plucking of hair.

steps.title: רב forbids unintended acts, but plucking is not shearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. רב forbids דבר שאין מתכוין. Plucking hair is not considered shearing. On יום טוב, plucking is uprooting done in an unusual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב really holds that an unintended act is forbidden. Plucking is not the same as shearing. On יום טוב, he permits clearing the hair because it counts as uprooting something from where it grows, done in an unusual way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that רב rules like רבי יהודה, so he forbids unintended acts. It now explains his lenient rulings in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, we thought רב permitted these acts because the result was unintended. Now the גמרא says that is not the reason. For a בכור, plucking is simply not the forbidden act of shearing (גזיזה). On יום טוב, the hair pulled out while clearing the spot with the cleaver is uprooted in an unusual way (כלאחר יד). That is not forbidden by Torah law, so the unintended plucking touches at most a rabbinic ban, and רב can permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (we return to the basic position)
One who plucks (pulls out by hand)
One who shears (cuts hair or wool)
Uprooting something from where it grows
In an unusual way, literally 'with the back of the hand'

steps.confusionAlert: רב is NOT permitting these acts because they are unintended. He agrees unintended acts are forbidden. He permits them because the act itself is not a Torah-level forbidden labor.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav actually holds:
an unintended act is forbidden,
and plucking is not the same as shearing,
phrases.notes: This explains why plucking a בכור's hair is allowed.

phrases.english: and on Yom Tov, this is the reason he permits it:

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ עוֹקֵר דָּבָר מִגִּידּוּלוֹ כִּלְאַחַר יָד.
phrases.english: because it is uprooting something from where it grows, done in an unusual way.
phrases.notes: A labor done in an unusual way is not forbidden by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4 by giving up the earlier explanation of רב and offering a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the permission comes from the nature of the act, not from lack of intent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב permitted these acts because he holds דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב forbids דבר שאין מתכוין. Plucking is not shearing, and on יום טוב the plucking is כלאחר יד.

steps.title: A ברייתא says plucking a feather counts as shearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that plucking is not shearing. A ברייתא says one who plucks a wing feather on שבת is liable, and ריש לקיש explains the liability is for shearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is plucking really not shearing? A ברייתא teaches: someone who plucks a wing feather, snips its tip, and strips off its threads must bring three sin offerings. ריש לקיש explained: plucking is liable as shearing, snipping as cutting, and stripping as smoothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new idea from Step 5 that plucking is not shearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says plucking a feather counts as the labor of shearing (גוזז). If plucking is shearing there, it should be shearing for a בכור's hair too. That would knock out the new answer about רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Wing (here, a large wing feather)
One who snips off the tip
One who strips or pulls off (the feather's threads)
Sin offering, brought for an accidental violation of שבת
One who smooths (a labor of שבת)

phrases.english: And plucking is not the same as shearing?
But it was taught in a baraita:
One who plucks the wing feather,
and snips its tip, and strips off its threads —
is liable to bring three sin offerings.
And Reish Lakish said:
one who plucks is liable for shearing,
phrases.notes: This is the part of the source that causes the difficulty.

phrases.english: one who snips is liable for cutting,
one who strips is liable for smoothing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one part of the answer in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that plucking (תולש) is not shearing (גוזז).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, as explained by ריש לקיש, treats plucking a feather as shearing on שבת. So plucking should count as shearing.

steps.title: Feathers are different because plucking is the normal way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a feather is different. Plucking is the normal way to remove feathers, so there it counts as shearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wing feather is different, because plucking is the normal way to remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 5 by showing why the feather case does not apply to hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A labor counts when it is done in its normal way. Feathers are normally removed by plucking, so plucking them is shearing. Hair is normally cut, not plucked, so plucking hair is not shearing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Its normal way

steps.whatToRemember: Plucking hair is not shearing, because hair is normally cut. Plucking feathers is shearing, because that is the normal way to remove feathers.

phrases.english: A wing is different, because that is its normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (אוקימתא of the source to its normal method).
steps.terutzMaskana: Plucking is shearing only where plucking is the normal method, as with feathers. It is not shearing for hair.

steps.title: Inference that רבי יוסי בן המשולם agrees with רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that since רב follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, רבי יוסי בן המשולם must agree with רב. That means he also forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רב holds like רבי יוסי בן המשולם, it follows that רבי יוסי בן המשולם holds like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a side conclusion from the new answer about רב. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ruled like רבי יוסי בן המשולם, who permits plucking a בכור's hair. According to Step 5, the reason is that plucking is not shearing, while unintended acts stay forbidden. So רבי יוסי בן המשולם should also hold that דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who permits plucking hair from a בכור to clear the slaughter spot
He holds like (agrees with)

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּרַב סָבַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם,
phrases.english: And since Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam holds like Rav,
phrases.notes: That is, he too forbids unintended acts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרַב סָבַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from the answer given in Steps 5 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי בן המשולם, like רב, must hold that דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden.

steps.title: The פרה אדומה case suggests רבי יוסי בן המשולם permits unintended acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוסי בן המשולם really forbids דבר שאין מתכוין. In a ברייתא about פרה אדומה, he lets one cut black hair tips with scissors and not worry about shearing a holy animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי בן המשולם really hold that an unintended act is forbidden? A ברייתא teaches: if a red heifer has two hairs that are red at the root and black at the top, רבי יוסי בן המשולם says one may cut them with scissors and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference of Step 8 with a ruling of רבי יוסי בן המשולם that seems to permit an unintended act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרה אדומה with two black hairs is disqualified. Cutting the black tips fixes this, but shearing a holy animal is normally forbidden. רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows it, which suggests he permits the unintended shearing because the goal is only to make the cow fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Red heifer; two black hairs disqualify it
Their roots are red
Their tops are black
Scissors
He need not be concerned

steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge stands, the new explanation of רב from Step 5 runs into trouble, because his source, רבי יוסי בן המשולם, would seem to permit unintended acts.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam hold
that an unintended act is forbidden?
But it was taught in a baraita:
Two hairs —
phrases.notes: On a red heifer, where two black hairs disqualify it.

phrases.english: whose roots are red and whose tops are black,
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
one cuts them with scissors and need not be concerned.
phrases.notes: He need not worry about the ban on shearing a holy animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין אָסוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי בן המשולם forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He permits cutting the black hair tips of a holy פרה אדומה without concern for the ban on shearing. This shows he permits an act whose forbidden result is unintended.

steps.title: A cow is not subject to shearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a פרה is different because shearing does not apply to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heifer is different, because it is not an animal that gets sheared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. It says cutting a פרה אדומה's hair is allowed because a cow is not an animal that gets sheared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If cows are not covered by the ban on shearing holy animals, then cutting the hair tips is not a ban at all. So this case would say nothing about דבר שאין מתכוין. רבי יוסי בן המשולם could still forbid it elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Cow or heifer (here, the פרה אדומה)
An animal that gets sheared

phrases.english: A heifer is different,
for it is not subject to shearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, דְּלָאו בַּת גִּיזָּה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (no shearing ban applies to cattle)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרה case shows that רבי יוסי בן המשולם permits דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרה case is irrelevant, because shearing does not apply to a cow.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows shearing applies to cattle too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the shearing ban and the work ban each apply to both cattle and sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not work with your firstborn ox, and do not shear your firstborn sheep.' From this I would only know that an ox may not be worked and a sheep may not be sheared. How do we know to apply each rule to the other animal too? The verse says 'Do not work... and do not shear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 10. It quotes a ברייתא that says the ban on shearing applies to oxen too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and' links the two parts of the פסוק, so both rules cover both animals. That means a cow is covered by the shearing ban. So the claim that a פרה cannot be sheared falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא?
Do not do work (with the animal)
Do not shear
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: "Do no work with the firstborn of your ox,
and do not shear the firstborn of your flock";
I would only know an ox regarding work
and sheep regarding shearing.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: From where do we apply what is said of this one to that one,
and what is said of that one to this one?
The verse says: "Do no work... and do not shear"!
phrases.notes: The 'and' joins both bans to both animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a פרה is not subject to shearing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא applies the shearing ban to cattle as well, so a cow is covered.

steps.title: The פרה has the holiness of בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a פרה אדומה has בדק הבית holiness, so the ban on shearing offerings does not apply to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a heifer is different, because it has the holiness of things set aside for Temple upkeep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first answer and gives a new one. The פרה אדומה is holy in the way בדק הבית items are holy, not in the way altar offerings are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרה is still holy. But the Torah's shearing ban is about animals holy for the altar. So the Torah's ban would not reach this kind of holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Things made holy for Temple upkeep (not for the altar)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the פרה is not holy. It has a different type of holiness, and the Torah's shearing ban does not cover that type.

phrases.english: Rather, a heifer is different,
for it is consecrated for Temple maintenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, דְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרה is covered by the shearing ban like other holy animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its בדק הבית holiness is not covered by the Torah's shearing ban.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר forbids shearing בדק הבית animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that בדק הבית animals may not be sheared or worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר said: things consecrated for Temple upkeep may not be sheared or worked!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 12. It quotes רבי אלעזר, who says even בדק הבית animals may not be sheared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בדק הבית animals are also banned from shearing, then the type of holiness does not help. Cutting the פרה's hair would still be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he not say?
Shearing and work

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
items consecrated for Temple maintenance
are forbidden in shearing and work!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אֲסוּרִין בְּגִיזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בדק הבית holiness frees the פרה from the shearing ban
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר applies the shearing ban to בדק הבית items too.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's ban is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The ban on shearing בדק הבית animals is only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is only a rabbinic ban.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's ban comes from the חכמים, not from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps Step 12 alive. By Torah law, the פרה is still not covered by the shearing ban.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrading the source of the ban
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ban is from the Torah.

steps.title: A rabbinic ban is still a ban
steps.stepSummary: Even a rabbinic ban should stop someone from cutting the hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still a rabbinic ban!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 14. A rabbinic ban still forbids the act, so why would רבי יוסי בן המשולם allow cutting the hair?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original question was why cutting is allowed at all. Calling the ban rabbinic does not make it permitted. So the בדק הבית answer still does not explain the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But there still is
A rabbinic prohibition

phrases.english: But there is still a rabbinic prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'only rabbinic' to permit the cutting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic ban still forbids the act, so the permission is still unexplained.

steps.title: A פרה אדומה is rare
steps.stepSummary: The rabbinic ban was not applied to the פרה אדומה because it is uncommon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a heifer is different, because it is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final new reason. A פרה אדומה is so rare that the חכמים did not extend their ban to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rabbinic bans usually target common situations. Since a פרה אדומה hardly ever happens, it was left out of רבי אלעזר's rabbinic ban. So cutting its hair is allowed, and this case says nothing about דבר שאין מתכוין.

keyTerms.meaning: Not common, rare

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects the idea from Step 8 that רבי יוסי בן המשולם forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.

phrases.english: Rather, a heifer is different,
for it is uncommon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after Step 15 weakens the previous one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rarity exemption from a rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rabbinic ban covers the פרה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים did not apply their ban to a case as rare as a פרה אדומה.

steps.title: Why not redeem it, shear it, and re-consecrate it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the owner doesn't take away the holiness, shear the animal, then make it holy again.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him redeem it and make it non-holy, shear it, and then consecrate it again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need to cut the hair while the animal is holy. There seems to be an easy way around the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a פרה has בדק הבית holiness, it can be redeemed. The owner could make it non-holy, cut the hair freely, and then consecrate it again. So why would רבי יוסי בן המשולם need to permit cutting while it is still holy?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him redeem it (remove its holiness)
Non-holy, ordinary
Let him consecrate it

phrases.english: But let him redeem it and bring it out to non-sacred status,
and shear it, and then consecrate it again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the leniency given in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to permit cutting a holy פרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeeming the animal first would avoid any ban, so no leniency should be needed.

steps.title: It is too expensive to redeem
steps.stepSummary: A פרה אדומה is worth so much that redeeming it is not practical.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its value is very high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that redeeming the פרה would cost a fortune, so we cannot expect the owner to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming means paying the animal's full value. A פרה אדומה is extremely expensive, so this workaround is not realistic.

keyTerms.meaning: Its price is expensive

phrases.english: Its price is expensive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17

steps.title: Use שמואל's rule and redeem it cheaply
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a holy item worth a מנה, redeemed on a פרוטה, is redeemed, so the cost is not a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him do as שמואל says. שמואל said: a holy item worth a hundred, redeemed on something worth a פרוטה, is redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 18. Using שמואל's rule, the owner could redeem the פרה for a tiny coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, redemption works even for far less than the item's value. If so, the high price does not matter. The workaround would be cheap and easy.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy (consecrated) item
A large sum (one hundred דינרים)
The smallest coin
Redeemed, made non-holy

phrases.english: But let him do with it like Shmuel,
for Shmuel said: a consecrated item worth a hundred dinars
that one redeemed onto a peruta's worth is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the high cost blocks redemption
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל allows redemption for a פרוטה, so cost is no obstacle.

steps.title: שמואל only meant after the fact
steps.stepSummary: שמואל only said the redemption works after it is done. He did not permit doing it that way from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that שמואל said it works once he redeemed it. Did he say one may do so from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל's rule is בדיעבד only. We cannot tell the owner to redeem the פרה cheaply לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheap redemption is valid once it happens, but it is not allowed as a plan. So the redemption workaround fails, and the rarity answer from Step 16 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: You can say
From the start, as a plan
Did he say?

phrases.english: Say that Shmuel said it holds once he redeemed it;
did he say it ab initio?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל שֶׁחִילְּלוֹ, לְכִתְחִלָּה מִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל allows cheap redemption as a plan.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל only validates it after the fact, so the rarity answer stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The first answer to Step 9: a פרה אדומה is rare, so the rabbinic shearing ban was not applied to it. That is why cutting its hair is allowed, even though רבי יוסי בן המשולם forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.

steps.title: רב follows him, but he does not follow רב
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: רב agrees with רבי יוסי בן המשולם on plucking, but רבי יוסי בן המשולם does not agree with רב on דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say: רב holds like רבי יוסי בן המשולם, but רבי יוסי בן המשולם does not hold like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to Step 9. It rejects the assumption from Step 8 that the two must agree on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם's ruling about plucking hair. That does not mean רבי יוסי בן המשולם shares רב's view on דבר שאין מתכוין. So he can permit דבר שאין מתכוין, and the פרה אדומה case causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces another answer)
Holds like

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to Step 9. (1) A פרה אדומה is rare, so it is an exception. (2) The agreement only goes one way: רב follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, but רבי יוסי בן המשולם may permit דבר שאין מתכוין.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם,
phrases.english: Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב.
phrases.english: but Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam does not hold like Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise of mutual agreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רב follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, the latter must also forbid דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The agreement is only one-way, so רבי יוסי בן המשולם can permit דבר שאין מתכוין.

steps.title: Plucking hair is allowed only by hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that one may pluck hair when slaughtering a בכור without moving it from its place. ריש לקיש says this is allowed only by hand, not with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And he plucks the hair, as long as he does not move it from its place.' רב אשי said in the name of ריש לקיש: This was taught only when done by hand. With a tool it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about plucking a בכור's hair at slaughter. ריש לקיש adds a limit: hand only, never a tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shearing a בכור is forbidden. Pulling some hair by hand to clear the spot for the knife does not look like shearing. Using a tool does look like shearing, so ריש לקיש forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: plucks / pulls out (by pulling)
move it from its place (fully remove the hair)
they only taught this (when...): a limiting formula
with a tool / utensil

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary between allowed plucking and forbidden 'shearing' of a בכור.

phrases.english: And he plucks the hair,
as long as he does not move it from its place.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said that Reish Lakish said:
They only taught this by hand,
but with a tool, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בַּיָּד, אֲבָל בִּכְלִי — אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, about plucking hair at slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plucking a בכור's hair at slaughter is permitted only by hand. With a tool it is forbidden.

steps.title: But the משנה mentions a cleaver
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: the משנה says one clears space 'with a cleaver' on both sides, which is a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught: 'He makes space with a cleaver from here and from there!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's rule using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said tools are forbidden. The משנה seems to allow clearing space with a cleaver, which is a tool. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it taught...? (opens a challenge from a source)
a cleaver / butcher's knife
from here and from there (on both sides)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
He makes space with a cleaver from here and from there!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's limit from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a tool is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly mentions a cleaver, which is a tool.

steps.title: Read it as 'for a cleaver'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading: one makes space by hand 'for' the cleaver, not 'with' the cleaver.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'for a cleaver.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by fixing one letter in the משנה: 'בקופיץ' (with a cleaver) becomes 'לקופיץ' (for a cleaver).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cleaver is the knife used to slaughter. One clears space for it by hand, so the משנה no longer mentions plucking with a tool, and ריש לקיש's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: teach / read (the text) as: a text correction
for the cleaver

steps.confusionAlert: The cleaver is still used, but only for slaughtering. The hair is cleared by hand to make room for it.

phrases.english: Teach: 'for a cleaver.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה permits clearing space with a cleaver, which is a tool.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means one clears space by hand for the cleaver, so tools stay forbidden.

steps.title: Is plucking to show a blemish allowed from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that one may pluck hair to see a מום, and asks whether this is allowed לכתחילה or only בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And likewise, one plucks the hair to see a blemish.' It was asked of them: Is this allowed from the start, or only after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and raises a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearly, once the hair was plucked, the examination is fine. The question is whether one may set out to pluck hair just to show the מום to a חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: a blemish (lets a בכור be slaughtered outside the מקדש)
it was asked of them: a real open question
from the start / allowed in advance
after the fact (it was done already)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תּוֹלֵשׁ אֶת הַשֵּׂעָר לִרְאוֹת מוּם.
phrases.english: And likewise, he plucks the hair to see a blemish.
It was asked of them:
From the start, or after the fact?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether plucking hair to show a מום is permitted לכתחילה or only בדיעבד.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוסי בן המשולם: allowed from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה brings a ברייתא: רבי יוסי בן המשולם says one plucks wool tangled in the ear and shows the מום. This proves it is allowed לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Come and hear: Wool tangled in the ear: רבי יוסי בן המשולם says he plucks it and shows the blemish. Learn from this: from the start. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question with a ברייתא, and the גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a direct instruction: 'pluck it and show.' That is a ruling for doing it in advance, not just accepting it afterward. So plucking to show a מום is allowed לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear: introduces a proof
tangled wool
learn from it: a conclusion is drawn

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Come and hear,
wool that is tangled in the ear:
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
He plucks it and shows its blemish.
Learn from it: from the start,
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That plucking hair to show a מום is permitted לכתחילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי בן המשולם: 'He plucks it and shows its blemish.'

steps.title: רב מרי: our משנה teaches it too
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says the same conclusion can be learned from the משנה itself, from the word 'וכן' (and likewise).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: We also learned this in our משנה: 'And likewise, one who plucks the hair to see the place of a blemish.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי opens a second proof, this time from our own משנה. This line sets up the analysis of the word 'וכן' that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי points to the word 'וכן', which links the blemish case to the earlier slaughter case. The next steps explain exactly which detail is being compared.

keyTerms.meaning: we too have learned it (in our משנה): extra support
and likewise: compares one case to another

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
We too have learned it as well,
And likewise, one who plucks the hair
to see the place of a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof to the conclusion of step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That plucking to show a מום is permitted לכתחילה.

steps.title: What does 'likewise' compare to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'וכן' refers to. It rejects the idea that it means 'don't move the hair,' because that would be obvious from the slaughter case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and likewise' mean? If you say it means he may not move it from its place, that is obvious: if even one who slaughters, whose slaughter shows his intent, may not move it, is it necessary to say so for one who looks at the place of a blemish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which detail 'וכן' is comparing, and rules out the first possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At slaughter, everyone can see he is not shearing the animal, yet he still may not remove the hair. So for just examining a מום, where nothing shows his intent, it would surely be forbidden too. The משנה would not need to teach that, so 'וכן' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say: introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
now (if even...): opens a 'how much more so' argument
proves about him (shows his intent)
is it needed (to say)? It's obvious

steps.confusionAlert: The 'obvious' logic runs from slaughter to the blemish case: slaughter is the easier case, so if it is forbidden there, it is surely forbidden for a blemish.

phrases.english: What is 'and likewise'?
If you say: that he may not move it from its place,
now, if one who slaughters,
whose slaughter shows his intent,
may not move it,
is it needed to say so for seeing the place of a blemish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the word 'וכן' that רב מרי cited in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which detail of the slaughter case 'וכן' compares to the blemish case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'וכן' as 'he may not move the hair from its place.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would teach something obvious from the slaughter case.

steps.title: 'Likewise' means plucking is allowed from the start
steps.stepSummary: So 'וכן' must refer to the permission to pluck. Just as plucking is allowed at slaughter, it is allowed לכתחילה to show a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it refer to plucking? Learn from it: from the start. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that 'וכן' compares the permission to pluck, which proves plucking to show a מום is allowed לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the 'don't move it' reading is ruled out, the only remaining comparison is the permission to pluck itself. Since plucking at slaughter is allowed in advance, plucking to show a מום is too.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, isn't it...? Leads to the only remaining option
regarding plucking

steps.whatToRemember: Plucking a בכור's hair is allowed by hand only (ריש לקיש). Plucking hair to show a מום to a חכם is allowed לכתחילה, proven from רבי יוסי בן המשולם and from the word 'וכן' in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it referring to plucking?
Learn from it: from the start,
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the only remaining reading after step 28 rejected the first one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Plucking hair to show a מום is permitted לכתחילה.

steps.title: New משנה: hair that fell off a blemished firstborn before slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes hair that fell off a בכור בעל מום while it was alive. The hair was put aside, and then the animal was slaughtered. עקביא בן מהללאל rules that the hair is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Hair fell off a בכור that has a מום. The owner put the hair away in a window-niche, and later he slaughtered the animal. עקביא בן מהללאל permits the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here with a case about hair that fell off a blemished בכור before it was slaughtered. It gives the first opinion, from עקביא בן מהללאל, who says the hair is permitted. This opens a dispute that continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור בעל מום may be slaughtered and eaten, but while it is alive you may not shear it or benefit from its wool. Once it is properly slaughtered, the hair on its body becomes permitted. The new question is about hair that fell off earlier, while the animal was still alive. עקביא בן מהללאל holds that the later slaughter makes this hair permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
A firstborn animal that has a permanent blemish, so it may be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש
That fell out or shed on its own
Here: a wall niche or compartment used for storage, not a window for light
A תנא from the early period of the משנה
Permits; rules that the item may be used

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here and think the halacha is settled. The משנה gives only עקביא בן מהללאל's opinion so far. The opposing opinion of the חכמים comes right after this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question for the rest of the sugya. Does slaughtering a בכור בעל מום permit only the hair still attached at death, or also hair that fell off earlier?

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Signals that a new משנה begins.

phrases.english: The hair of a blemished firstborn that fell off,
phrases.notes: The hair came off while the animal was still alive.

phrases.english: and he placed it in a niche,
phrases.notes: He put it aside for safekeeping.

phrases.english: and afterward he slaughtered it (the animal):
phrases.notes: The slaughter happened after the hair had already fallen off.

phrases.english: Akavya ben Mahalalel permits it,
phrases.notes: First opinion in the dispute. The other view follows.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׂעַר בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנָּשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic. It follows the end of the previous discussion about plucking hair to show a מום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עקביא בן מהללאל, hair that fell off a בכור בעל מום while it was alive, and was set aside, is permitted once the animal is slaughtered.
